study: Phase 3 & Phase 4: Parameterized 190.53V/416V 50Hz Transformer Interface and 24h QSTS Scenarios
timescale_separation_rule: 6.5 s local ODE transients and 24-hour 1-minute QSTS network power flows are strictly separated. The 6.5 s trajectory is never extrapolated to 24 h. Steady-state PCC power from the 50 Hz VSG (p_ss_kw = 2.852527 kW) is evaluated as a one-way static snapshot, while 24 h QSTS uses explicit synthetic profiles.

phase3_transformer_design_hypotheses.unbalance_and_winding_findings: Because the IEEE European LV feeder is unbalanced, connecting a 3-phase transformer with delta on the inverter side and grounded-wye on the 416 V grid side (Dyn) creates a zero-sequence sink that draws ~0.542 A of zero-sequence current from the feeder and skews per-phase grid power (0.931 / 1.122 / 0.914 kW). Conversely, grounded-wye/grounded-wye (YNyn0) or grounded-wye/ungrounded-delta (Ynd) keeps phase power injection nearly balanced (~0.989 kW/phase after ~38.7 W copper loss at 3 kW).

phase4_qsts_24h_scenarios.solar_profile_provenance: Synthetic 06:00-18:00 half-sine (peak 3.0 kW at noon), NOT measured irradiance
phase4_qsts_24h_scenarios.bess_profile_provenance: Energy-consistent synthetic daily shaving hypothesis (charges 09:00-15:00 up to 1.0 kW, discharges 17:00-21:00 up to 1.354 kW with eta=0.95 per way, Delta SoC_24h = 0, throughput ~3.82 kWh). Explicitly labeled as a scaled bank hypothesis; the single 2p Leaf cell pair (~0.165 kWh) remains blocked by BAT26-48 for kWh-scale feeder dispatch until N_s x N_p is approved.
